answer: In an agent economy routing timber freight through a port jetty, Sybil resistance relies on hardware enclave attestation. When nodes exchange state over a whisper protocol, each agent must present cryptographic quotes signed by an onboard secure cryptoprocessor. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of procuring discrete physical chips per identity. However, microarchitectural side-channel leaks can expose enclave signing keys, letting adversaries forge proofs on commodity hardware.
